result.summary: This PR introduces util::NotNull<SmartPtrType>, a wrapper type modeled on gsl::strict_not_null that documents and enforces at compile time (with a one-time runtime Assert at construction) that a smart pointer can never be null. It is applied to several existing call sites — CDBWrapper's LevelDBContext, CNode's Transport, CTxMemPool::GetChangeSet, and CoinsViewOverlay's thread pool — to replace scattered per-access Assert() calls with a stronger, self-documenting type. The PR includes a large new unit test file exercising the type's construction, comparison, move, and thread-safety-annotation behavior.
result.problem: The C++ standard library has no idiom for a smart pointer guaranteed non-null; code either relies on manual Assert() calls scattered at every dereference or on comments, both of which are easy to miss or duplicate. This affects maintainers who want compile-time-checked invariants instead of runtime checks sprinkled through the code, as referenced in the long-standing issue #24423.

open_concerns: A handful of nits remain about move semantics, LIFETIMEBOUND annotations, and constructor ambiguity but were resolved in the final pushes.

Several reviewers (l0rinc) suggested extending NotNull to more call sites (GetWalletForJSONRPCRequest, BlockTemplateImpl, AddrMan, TxRequestTracker) but author and reviewers agreed these are follow-ups, not blockers.
resolved_concerns: l0rinc's concern about verbose call sites addressed via NotNullUniquePtr/NotNullSharedPtr aliases.
stickies-v's forwarding-constructor ambiguity issue fixed by adding a requires clause excluding NotNull-to-NotNull construction.
Debate over whether NotNull should be movable resolved by author adding move-support commits after discussion.
l0rinc's request to base the header more closely on upstream GSL evolved into a full custom rewrite (with stickies-v's prototype) that the author adopted, addressing complexity/attribution concerns.

result.card: This PR adds util::NotNull<SmartPtrType>, a compile-time-checked wrapper documenting that a smart pointer is never null, replacing scattered runtime Assert() calls, and applies it to a handful of existing members (LevelDBContext in CDBWrapper, CNode's Transport, CTxMemPool::GetChangeSet, CoinsViewOverlay's thread pool). It solves a general maintainability problem (issue #24423) rather than any observed bug, so its impact in each touched area (indexes, mempool, p2p, validation) is limited to a type-safety cleanup with no behavioral change. Its main and most durable value is in the utils category, as a new reusable safety primitive that could reduce repeated Assert patterns project-wide if adopted more broadly, which reviewers explicitly deferred to follow-up PRs. The PR received deep, sustained review from stickies-v and l0rinc over roughly five months, with all raised issues (constructor ambiguity, movability, verbosity, GSL basis) resolved, and stickies-v gave a final ACK on the latest commit. No dependency blocks this PR, and it is Ready for review with no open blocking concerns.
